papers.title: Spatial transcriptomics resolves ductal TREM2+ and stromal FOLR2+ macrophages in the normal human breast at microanatomical resolution
papers.authors: Kim, E. K., Le, J. T., Moser, B. A., Phong, K. T., Gartner, Z. J.
papers.abstract: Macrophage identities are coupled to specialized roles through their local niches of residence. In the breast, macrophages contribute to epithelial development and remodeling, immune surveillance, and angiogenesis. These diverse functions imply a spatial organization of distinct transcriptional states. Yet, how this heterogeneity is spatially arranged in the normal human breast at microanatomical
summary_bullets: Spatial transcriptomics reveals two distinct macrophage populations in human breast: ductal TREM2+ and stromal FOLR2+ macrophages with niche-specific identities.
Macrophage transcriptional states are spatially organized according to microanatomical location, coupling their identity to specialized functions in epithelial and stromal compartments.
High-resolution mapping demonstrates macrophage heterogeneity reflects their roles in breast development, immune surveillance, and angiogenesis within distinct tissue niches.

papers.title: RVQ-Alpha: Bridging Single-Cell Transcriptomics and Large Language Models via Hierarchical Discrete Tokenization and Fact-Aware Reinforcement Learning
papers.authors: Li, G., You, Y., Fu, Y., Zhou, W., Tang, F., Kong, J., Tian, L.
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing yields continuous expression profiles, whereas large language models operate over discrete autoregressive sequences, leaving no shared computational interface for language-model reasoning over cell states. Existing approaches either keep cellular information outside the LLM vocabulary, consume context per listed gene, or learn reconstruction codes without gene-level grou
summary_bullets: Proposes hierarchical discrete tokenization converting continuous single-cell RNA data into LLM-compatible tokens, enabling direct language model reasoning over cell states.
Introduces fact-aware reinforcement learning to align generated biological insights with known gene relationships and cellular knowledge.
Achieves efficient representation with reduced context consumption while maintaining interpretability of gene-level information.

papers.title: jazzPanda: spatially aware marker gene detection for imaging-based spatial transcriptomics
papers.authors: Jin, X., Putri, G. H., Cheng, J., Asselin-Labat, M.-L., Smyth, G. K., Phipson, B.
papers.abstract: Motivation: Spatial transcriptomics resolves the organisation of tissues and their cellular neighbourhoods, where cell type identification depends on reliable marker gene detection. Existing marker methods were developed for single-cell RNA sequencing and ignore the spatial coordinates of cells and transcripts, a particular problem for imaging-based platforms where transcript counts per gene per c
summary_bullets: Existing marker gene methods ignore spatial structure; jazzPanda incorporates spatial coordinates for improved cell-type identification in imaging-based spatial transcriptomics.
Novel spatially-aware approach outperforms single-cell methods by leveraging transcript location information specific to imaging platforms.
Method addresses low transcript counts per gene in imaging data where spatial context becomes critical for accurate marker detection.

papers.title: PANCS-Inhibitors: A rapid method to directly select for protein-protein interaction inhibitors
papers.authors: Styles, M. J., Xie, V. C., Legault, S., Pixley, J. A., Dickinson, B. C.
papers.abstract: Aberrant protein-protein interactions (PPIs) drive myriad diseases. Inhibiting these PPIs often relies on discovering molecules that bind to one of the proteins and hoping that this binding inhibits the PPI. Molecular binder discovery often takes months, but a discovery process that ensures that the resulting molecule not only binds a target protein, but selectively inhibits a target PPI, could dr
summary_bullets: PANCS-Inhibitors enables direct selection for molecules that both bind target proteins AND inhibit specific protein-protein interactions simultaneously.
Method accelerates PPI inhibitor discovery by eliminating need to screen binding molecules separately for functional inhibition.
Rapid selection approach could reduce timeline from months to faster discovery of disease-relevant PPI inhibitors.

papers.title: Structural basis for alternative 3' splice site selection in the human spliceosome active center
papers.authors: Marciano, G., Eckert, S., Zuvanonv, L., Miyagawa, T., Yang, L., Datcu, G., Sheng, Y., Kwon, H. Y., Cameron, L., Heyd, F. M., Fica, S. M.
papers.abstract: Accurate alternative splicing requires discrimination between adjacent 3' splice sites (3'-ss) during catalysis and is disrupted by pathogenic AG-gain mutations that create competing 3'-ss. Here, we present cryo-EM structures of human spliceosomes assembled on native-sequence pre-mRNAs, revealing how the catalytic core controls alternative 3'-ss selection. SDE2 is a previously unrecognized active-
summary_bullets: SDE2 protein controls 3' splice site selection by stabilizing catalytic metal ions and discriminating between competing sites.
AG-gain mutations create pathogenic alternative 3' sites by disrupting SDE2-mediated discrimination mechanisms in the spliceosome.
Cryo-EM structures reveal molecular basis for how spliceosome active center selects correct 3' splice site during catalysis.

papers.title: Short Linear Motifs as a General Organizing Principle of the Nuclear-Receptor Proximal Interactome
papers.authors: Eng, J. K., Radoshevich, L., Wright, M. E.
papers.abstract: The AR-interactome comprises ~1,000 androgen receptor-interacting proteins (AR-IPs), yet how a single receptor engages so many partners across compartments remains mechanistically unclear. We integrate proximity-labeling quantitative mass spectrometry across cytosolic, microsomal, and nuclear compartments of LNCaP prostate cancer cells and resolve 4,751 AR-proximal interacting proteins (AR-PIPs),
summary_bullets: Short linear motifs (SLiMs) organize AR's proximal interactome across cellular compartments, enabling efficient engagement of ~4,700+ proteins.
Compartment-specific SLiM patterns dictate AR protein interactions, revealing how single receptor coordinates diverse signaling in cytosol, microsome, and nucleus.
SLiMs function as general organizing principle for nuclear receptor proximal interactomes, providing mechanistic explanation for extensive protein engagement networks.

papers.title: High-Specificity Detection of Chromosomal Mosaicism Reveals Cell-Type-Specific Genomic Alteration Patterns in Aging Tissues
papers.authors: Chen, X. E., Wang, H., Yang, Y., Teneche, M. G., Adams, P. D., Wilson, P., Zhang, N.
papers.abstract: Mosaic chromosomal alterations (mCAs) increase with age and are associated with multiple diseases, yet the cell types and states that harbor these alterations remain largely unknown. Because mCAs arise in individual cells prior to clonal expansion, they are typically rare and obscured in bulk data. We develop CHASM, a method for detecting chromosomal copy number alterations (CNA) from single-cell
summary_bullets: CHASM detects rare mosaic chromosomal alterations in single cells, revealing age-associated CNA patterns previously hidden in bulk sequencing data.
Cell-type-specific genomic alteration patterns emerge with aging, enabling identification of which tissue cell populations accumulate chromosomal mosaicism.
Single-cell resolution uncovers clonal expansion of individual mCAs, clarifying disease mechanisms linked to age-related chromosomal alterations.

papers.title: Invasion status stratifies the composition of the human pancreatic cancer perineural niche
papers.authors: Hussain, Z., Yarlagadda, D. V. K., Li, Q., Tezcan, N., Stupakov, P., Sadatrezaei, G., Wong, R. J., Massague, J., Tarcan, Z., Basturk, O., Deborde, S., Leslie, C. S., Sherman, M. H.
papers.abstract: The peripheral nervous system innervates the pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) microenvironment, and perineural invasion (PNI), the invasion of cancer cells in and around nerves, correlates with metastatic burden and poor outcomes. Though PDAC innervation is near universal and the majority of PDAC patients harbor PNI, the cellular and molecular composition of the heterocellular perineural ni
summary_bullets: Perineural invasion (PNI) is common in PDAC and linked to worse outcomes, but its cellular composition was unclear.
The study profiles how invasion status changes the cell types present in the perineural niche.
Findings point to niche-specific targets tied to nerve invasion in pancreatic cancer.

papers.title: A Temporal Atlas of the Nuclear Androgen Receptor Proximal Interactome
papers.authors: Ptak, C. C., Eng, J., Radoshevich, L., Wright, M. E.
papers.abstract: Androgen receptor-interacting proteins (AR-IPs) comprise nearly 1,000 cataloged partners, yet how AR engages this interactome inside the nucleus, in what temporal order, and through what molecular handoffs, remains uncharted. Here, we construct a minute-scale temporal atlas of the nuclear AR proximal interactome by proximity-labeling quantitative mass spectrometry (PL-qMS) in androgen-treated LNCa
summary_bullets: AR recruits ~1,000 interacting proteins in temporally-ordered, sequential waves during nuclear activation, revealing dynamic handoff mechanisms.
Proximity-labeling mass spectrometry maps minute-scale kinetics of AR proximal interactome, showing distinct temporal recruitment phases.
Nuclear AR engagement follows defined temporal order, providing mechanistic insight into androgen receptor signaling dynamics.

papers.title: A Spatiotemporal Atlas of Extranuclear Androgen Receptor Proximal Interaction Networks
papers.authors: Ptak, C. C., O'Rourke, C., Eng, J., Radoshevich, L., Wright, M. E.
papers.abstract: Androgen receptor-interacting proteins (AR-IPs) comprise nearly 1,000 proteins, yet their organization across subcellular space and time remains uncharted. Proximity labeling captures direct binding partners along with neighboring proteins that populate a receptor's local environment, thereby broadening AR-IPs into a broader population of AR-proximal interacting proteins (AR-PIPs). Here, we apply
summary_bullets: Proximity labeling reveals ~1,000 androgen receptor-proximal proteins organized in distinct subcellular compartments and temporal patterns.
AR-proximal interaction networks extend beyond direct binding partners to include neighboring proteins in local microenvironments.
Spatiotemporal mapping provides comprehensive atlas of AR signaling landscape across different cellular locations and time points.

papers.title: A simple method for analyzing competitive growth of multiple cell types in xenograft tumors
papers.authors: Melhuish, T. A., Adair, S. J., Pemberton, O. S., Bauer, T. W., Wotton, D.
papers.abstract: Low take rates and inter-tumor variability in growth rates can limit the effectiveness of mouse xenograft models when comparing between groups. To address this problem we developed a simple method to compare multiple cell types within a single mixed xenograft. Individual cell lines or clones were transduced with a lentiviral vector that includes a unique PCR tag, allowing the use of qPCR to determ
summary_bullets: Mixed xenografts with unique PCR tags enable direct quantification of competitive growth between multiple cell types within single tumors.
Method reduces variability and low take rates by comparing cell types internally rather than across separate animals.
qPCR-based tracking of lentiviral barcodes provides simple, scalable approach for measuring clonal competition dynamics in vivo.

papers.title: PURPL is associated with adverse clinical outcome in Luminal A breast cancer
papers.authors: Ochoa Zavalza, S. J., Pouokam, M., Kruse, M., Gonzalez-Isunza, G., Sazdanovic, R., Arsuaga, J.
papers.abstract: Introduction: Luminal A is the most common breast cancer molecular subtype and is generally associated with a favorable five-year prognosis. However, a substantial subset of patients experience relapse, suggesting that biologically distinct high-risk tumors exist within this subtype. Methods: We applied Topological Analysis of Array Comparative Genomic Hybridization (TAaCGH) to identify recurrent
summary_bullets: PURPL genomic abnormality identifies high-risk Luminal A breast cancer patients who experience relapse despite generally favorable prognosis.
Topological CGH analysis reveals biologically distinct, aggressive tumors within clinically favorable Luminal A subtype requiring stratification.
PURPL status could improve patient risk stratification and treatment decisions in Luminal A breast cancer management.

papers.title: EpiBench: Can LLMs Understand Epitopes for Antibody Drug Discovery?
papers.authors: Zirui Wang, Jiaqi Wang, Qinghan Wang, Yuzhi Xu, Gang Du, Tingjun Hou, Odin Zhang
papers.abstract: Epitopes determine where antibodies bind antigens and shape downstream therapeutic properties such as functional blockade and escape resistance, making epitope understanding central to antibody drug discovery. Although large language models (LLMs) have shown strong biomedical reasoning ability, it remains unclear whether they can infer epitope information directly from antigen and antibody sequenc
summary_bullets: LLMs struggle to predict epitope information from antigen-antibody sequences alone, limiting their direct application in antibody drug discovery workflows.
EpiBench benchmark reveals performance gaps between LLMs and specialized structural prediction methods for epitope understanding tasks.
Current LLMs lack sufficient structural reasoning to infer binding site properties critical for therapeutic antibody development.

papers.title: The Virtual Tissues foundation model resolves spatial proteomics across scales
papers.authors: Wenckstern J, Jain E, von Querfurth B, Cheng Y, Vasilev K, Pariset M, Cheng PF, Liakopoulos P, Michielin O, Wicki A, Gut G, Bunne C.
papers.abstract: Spatial proteomics technologies have transformed our understanding of complex tissue architecture in cancer but present unique challenges for computational analysis<sup>1</sup>. Each study uses a different marker panel and protocol, and most methods are tailored to single cohorts, which limits knowledge transfer and robust biomarker discovery. Here we present Virtual Tissues (VirTues), a general-p
summary_bullets: VirTues foundation model enables cross-cohort spatial proteomics analysis despite different marker panels and protocols.
Single unified framework transfers knowledge across studies, improving biomarker discovery and tissue architecture understanding.
Resolves multi-scale spatial proteomics data, addressing computational challenges in cancer tissue analysis.

papers.title: A compendium of next-generation patient-derived models for diverse cancers
papers.authors: ElHarouni D, Al-Jazrawe M, Choi S, Dede M, Hinoue T, Misek SA, Noh H, Zanella L, Tseng YY, Francies HE, Plenker D, Kyi CW, Perez-Mayoral J, Stine MJ, Tonsing-Carter E, Agarwal R, Zenklusen JC, Clinton JM, Shelton JM, Chu TR, Hooper WF, Loinaz X, Keskula P, Tagle J, Kuhlers PC, Tercan B, Boj SF, Vasciaveo A, Tomassoni L, Crawford JM, Walsh S, Sinai C, Bhatia S, Sridevi P, Patel H, Cerone MA, HCMI Network, Ellrott K, Kuo CJ, Elemento O, Beyaz S, Corbo V, Spector DL, Beroukhim R, Ferguson ML, Cherniack AD, Laird PW, Robine N, McPherson A, Hoadley KA, Garnett MJ, Tuveson DA, Califano A, Spellman PT, Ligon KL, Gerhard DS, Staudt LM, Boehm JS.
papers.abstract: The development of new therapeutics and the validation of pathogenetic cancer mechanisms require representative laboratory models<sup>1,2</sup>. However, existing collections represent only a fraction of the diversity observed in human cancer<sup>2-4</sup>. Recent technologies have enabled efficient in vitro model derivation (for example, tumour organoids)<sup>5</sup>. However, whether these maint
summary_bullets: Patient-derived organoids and next-generation models now enable efficient laboratory derivation capturing broader cancer diversity than traditional cell lines.
These representative models validate pathogenic mechanisms and support therapeutic development across multiple cancer types.
New technologies provide practical tools for researchers to generate diverse cancer models reflecting human tumor heterogeneity.

papers.title: Spatial biology reveals altered macrophage states in immunosuppressed non-melanoma skin cancer
papers.authors: Naara S, Kochat V, Rao X, Arslan E, Saddawi-Konefka R, Satpati S, Garbarino J, Anderson JL, Gleber-Netto FO, Nagarajan P, Kerr TD, Akhter S, Li S, Fodor R, Koyfman SA, Yaniv D, Xie T, Glaun M, Bobian M, Padron WI, Ng C, Gunaratne PH, Thevasagayampillai S, Migden MR, Abbas HA, Reville PK, Tsai KY, McGrail DJ, Wang J, Myers JN, Gross ND, Rai K, Amit M.
papers.abstract: Immunosuppressed patients with non-melanoma skin cancer experience worse clinical outcomes, yet the tumor immune microenvironment associated with systemic immunosuppression remains incompletely defined. Using integrated single-cell, spatial transcriptomic, multiplex immunofluorescence, and spatial epigenomic profiling across immunocompetent and immunosuppressed tumors, we found that overall immune
summary_bullets: Immunosuppression alters macrophage states in non-melanoma skin cancer, contributing to worse clinical outcomes through microenvironment changes.
Spatial transcriptomics reveals distinct immune cell positioning and functional states differ between immunocompetent versus immunosuppressed tumors.
Integrated multi-omics approach identifies macrophage dysfunction as key driver of immunosuppression-related tumor progression.

papers.title: Dynamic prediction of HIV-related incomplete immune reconstitution: A multicenter, large cohort study using advanced joint modeling
papers.authors: Liu F, Zhang H, Wang X, Huang J, Shi J, Yang Z, Bao J, Zhao H, Pu C, Wang S, Xu A, Wang M, Yan D, Li Y, Sun R, Sheng H, Yu J, Zhang F, Sun L.
papers.abstract: Incomplete immune reconstitution (IIR) is a serious complication affecting 10 to 40% of people living with HIV (PLWH) despite effective antiretroviral therapy, leading to increased morbidity and mortality. Current risk prediction models rely on single-time point measurements and lack dynamic assessment capabilities. We developed a dynamic joint prediction system for IIR risk (DJPSIIR) using Bayesi
summary_bullets: Incomplete immune reconstitution affects 10-40% of people with HIV despite effective antiretroviral therapy.
Built a dynamic joint-modeling system (DJPSIIR) using repeated measurements instead of single time points.
Aims to give clinicians better, continuously updated risk prediction for IIR.

papers.title: Leveraging IGF signaling to improve the spatial organization and regenerative potential of iPSC-derived vascularized liver organoids
papers.authors: Kim DH, Lee Y, Kim MJ, Lee AC, Kwon S, Kang KS.
papers.abstract: Liver tissue engineering offers a promising alternative for end-stage liver disease, yet the recreation of functional vasculature remains a major bottleneck to clinical translation. Here, we developed vascularized liver organoids by integrating human induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived hepatoblasts and endothelial cells into decellularized scaffolds functionalized with an anti-CD31 aptame
summary_bullets: Engineered vascularized liver organoids from iPSC-derived hepatoblasts and endothelial cells on functionalized scaffolds.
IGF signaling improves spatial organization of the vasculature within the organoid.
Enhances regenerative potential, a step toward liver tissue engineering for end-stage liver disease.

papers.title: Assessing pedestrian responses to autonomous and personal mobility robots in crowded public spaces
papers.authors: Wojcikiewicz D, Billard A, Paez-Granados D.
papers.abstract: Robots increasingly share spaces with people, supporting delivery services and mobility for the aging populations, yet their ability to share space comfortably lacks understanding and benchmarks for designers and policy-makers. We compared human-robot (HRI) and human-human (HHI) interactions across four real-world crowd datasets spanning Europe, North America, and Asia, using a unified pipeline to
summary_bullets: Compared human-robot and human-human interactions across four real-world crowd datasets on three continents.
Used a unified analysis pipeline to benchmark how pedestrians respond to autonomous/personal mobility robots.
Offers empirical benchmarks to guide robot design and public-space policy.

papers.title: FLIP is essential for oncogenic KRAS-driven lung cancer
papers.authors: Hamilton, C., Sharkey, S., Khawaja, H., Downs, M., McLaughlin, C., Brown, C. N., Doherty, D., Fox, J., Pettigrew, M., Butterworth, K., Phillips, A., Small, D., Harrison, T., Higgins, C., Kerr, E. M., Longley, D. B.
papers.abstract: Mutations in KRAS represent the most common oncogenic event in human cancer and occur in approximately 30% of lung adenocarcinomas. The mechanisms by which lung tumours evade apoptosis induced by oncogenic KRAS-driven stress remain incompletely understood. Here, we identify the anti-apoptotic regulator FLIP (CFLAR) as a critical dependency in KRAS-mutant lung cancers. We demonstrate that KRAS-muta
summary_bullets: FLIP (CFLAR) is essential for survival of KRAS-mutant lung cancer cells and represents a critical therapeutic dependency
Oncogenic KRAS-driven tumors rely on FLIP to evade apoptosis triggered by KRAS-induced cellular stress
FLIP inhibition offers a potential therapeutic strategy for treating KRAS-mutant lung adenocarcinomas

papers.title: Senescent peripheral fibroblasts initiate chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy
papers.authors: Malachowski, T., Raut, G., Ren, Q., Mishra, R., Bagchi, S. M., Deavers, D., Luo, X., Staff, N., Price, T. J., Haroutounian, S., Stewart, S.
papers.abstract: Chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy (CIPN) is a common, debilitating complication of cancer therapy. Although axonal degeneration defines CIPN, the initiating cellular events remain unknown. Here, we show that CIPN is initiated by senescent peripheral fibroblasts rather than by the neuron itself. Across the mechanistically distinct chemotherapeutic agents paclitaxel and cisplatin, chemother
summary_bullets: Senescent peripheral fibroblasts, not neurons, initiate chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy across different chemotherapy agents.
CIPN pathogenesis originates from non-neuronal cells in the peripheral microenvironment rather than intrinsic axonal damage.
Fibroblast senescence represents a novel therapeutic target for preventing chemotherapy-induced neuropathy complications.

papers.title: The coumarin derivative X6632 is a pan-ID protein inhibitor that suppresses tumor growth by targeting cancer cells and the tumor-associated microvasculature
papers.authors: Götz, L. S., Deo, A., Scherer, S. D., D'Antonio, L., Weber, H. T., Sedlmeier, G., Torre Flores, L. P., Kaiser, U., Far, E., Raviv, Z., Thiele, W., Thaler, S., Jung, N., Bräse, S., Hill, C. S., Welm, A. L., Shaked, Y., Garvalov, B. K., Sleeman, J. P.
papers.abstract: Inhibitor of DNA binding (ID) proteins are key regulators of tumor cell stemness, therapy resistance and pathological angiogenesis in multiple cancer types and other diseases. Here, we characterize the coumarin-derived compound X6632 as a pan-ID inhibitor with dual activity against tumor cells and the tumor-associated microvasculature in a number of human and murine models. X6632 efficiently suppr
summary_bullets: X6632 coumarin compound inhibits all ID proteins, reducing tumor growth in multiple cancer models.
Dual mechanism: X6632 targets both cancer cells and tumor-associated blood vessel formation simultaneously.
ID protein inhibition overcomes therapy resistance and suppresses cancer stem cell properties.

papers.title: The CTCF Paralog BORIS Contributes to the Ovarian Cancer Transcriptional Program by Relaxing CTCF-mediated 3D Genome Organization
papers.authors: Bhatt, D. N., Scott, A., Krymskaya, L., Markowitz, T. E., Price, E., Ji, Y., Loukinov, D., Traver, M., Brzostowski, J., Lobanenkov, V. V., Pugacheva, E. M.
papers.abstract: Disruption of three-dimensional genome architecture is a major driver of cancer initiation and progression, frequently arising from genetic and epigenetic alterations at CTCF- and cohesin-bound chromatin anchors. These same chromatin loop anchors can also be occupied by the germ cell-specific CTCF paralog CTCFL (BORIS), which is aberrantly activated in multiple malignancies. Here, we show that in
summary_bullets: BORIS aberrantly replaces CTCF at chromatin loop anchors in ovarian cancer, disrupting 3D genome organization and driving oncogenic transcription.
BORIS-mediated relaxation of CTCF-imposed topological constraints alters enhancer-promoter contacts, rewiring the cancer transcriptional program.
BORIS activation represents an epigenetic mechanism of genome architecture disruption contributing to ovarian cancer progression.

papers.title: Endocytosis of ALK promotes glucose uptake in ALK-amplified neuroblastoma
papers.authors: Tsutsumi, R., Hikage, S., Kiyonari, S., Sakai, R.
papers.abstract: Activated receptor tyrosine kinases (RTKs), such as epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) and anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK), trigger intracellular signaling while undergoing receptor endocytosis. We recently identified a noncanonical mechanism in which RTK-containing endocytic vesicles deliver extracellular glucose to hexokinases associated with the outer mitochondrial membrane, thereby promo
summary_bullets: ALK endocytosis in neuroblastoma cells delivers extracellular glucose to mitochondrial hexokinases via endocytic vesicles, promoting glucose uptake.
This noncanonical mechanism links RTK endocytosis directly to metabolic function independent of traditional signaling pathways.
ALK-amplified neuroblastoma exploits this endocytic glucose delivery to support metabolic demands.

papers.title: MolX: A Geometric Foundation Model for Protein-Ligand Modelling
papers.authors: Liu, J., Pan, T., Guo, X., Ran, Z., Hao, Y., Yang, Y., Ng, A. P., Pan, S., Song, J., Li, F.
papers.abstract: Understanding how small molecules interact with protein binding pockets is central to structure-based drug discovery. Accurately modelling these interactions requires capturing the 3D geometry and physicochemical complementarity of binding interfaces, yet existing computational approaches encode proteins and ligands separately or rely on simplified structural representations that do not explicitly
summary_bullets: Foundation model using 3D geometric representations for accurate protein-ligand interaction prediction and drug discovery applications.
Unified encoding of proteins and ligands captures complementarity better than separate or simplified structural approaches.
Enables improved structure-based drug discovery through explicit geometric and physicochemical binding interface modeling.

papers.title: VRK1 kinase maintains an undifferentiated proliferative state in neuroblastoma tumor cells
papers.authors: Ojeda-Puertas, M., Gomez Munoz, M. d. l. A., Colmenero-Repiso, A., Amador-Alvarez, A., Rodriguez-Prieto, I., Pardal, R., Vega, F. M.
papers.abstract: Neuroblastoma is a neural crest-derived pediatric malignancy characterized by marked cellular heterogeneity and variable differentiation status. Undifferentiated tumors are associated with aggressive clinical behavior, treatment resistance and poor outcome, highlighting the need to identify molecular mechanisms that sustain tumor cell plasticity and prevent differentiation. Vaccinia-related kinase
summary_bullets: VRK1 kinase sustains undifferentiated, proliferative states in neuroblastoma cells, preventing terminal differentiation.
VRK1 represents a therapeutic target for promoting differentiation and overcoming aggressive tumor behavior in neuroblastoma.
Blocking VRK1 may reduce cellular plasticity and increase treatment sensitivity in undifferentiated neuroblastoma tumors.

papers.title: Frozen but Not Always Accessible: A Representation Analysis of Genomic Language Models
papers.authors: Nirjhor Datta, Swakkhar Shatabda, M. Sohel Rahman
papers.abstract: Genomic foundation models are increasingly reused as frozen feature extractors for downstream sequence prediction, offering a compute-efficient alternative to full fine-tuning. However, it remains unclear when biological information encoded by these models is accessible without task-specific adaptation. We present a representation-accessibility analysis of frozen genomic language models across reg
summary_bullets: Frozen genomic language models encode biological information but accessibility varies by task; not always readily available without adaptation.
Representation analysis reveals biological features require task-specific mechanisms to extract, limiting compute-efficient frozen feature extraction effectiveness.
Information present in frozen models doesn't guarantee accessibility for downstream predictions without proper adaptation strategies.

papers.title: Distinct cellular phenotypes of language and executive decline in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.
papers.authors: Petrescu J, Gouveia Roque C, Jackson CA, Daly AC, Butti Z, Kang K, Casel O, Leung M, Reilly L, Eschbach J, Gebremedhin B, McDade K, Gregory JM, Bonneau R, Smith C, Phatnani H.
papers.abstract: Cognitive manifestations, including impairments in language and executive functions, are seen in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. We mapped prefrontal cortex regions from ALS patients by integrating spatial and single-nucleus transcriptomics in a cognitively stratified patient cohort. We uncover that cognitive impairment in ALS is associated with d
summary_bullets: Mapped prefrontal cortex regions in ALS patients using combined spatial and single-nucleus transcriptomics.
Cognitive impairment (language/executive decline) in ALS is associated with distinct cellular changes.
Stratified cohort by cognitive status to link specific cell states to specific symptoms.

papers.title: Divergent impacts of explainable AI for dermatological diagnosis on clinicians versus lay people
papers.authors: Xu X', Hu H, Zhang H, Wang WK, Wang R, Soenksen LR, Badri O, Jafry S, Burger E, Nwandu L, Mehta A, Duhaime EP, Qasim A, Lin H, Pereira JK, Hershon J, Mui P, Gru AA, Elhadad N, Mamykina L, Groh M, Tschandl P, Daneshjou R, Ghassemi M.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly permeating healthcare, from serving as a physician assistant to powering consumer applications. The opacity of AI algorithms makes the ability of humans to interact with AI algorithms challenging. To overcome this limitation, explainable AI (XAI) provides insight into AI decision-making, but evidence suggests that XAI can paradoxically induce bias in th
summary_bullets: Explainable AI (XAI) is meant to make AI decisions more transparent in dermatology diagnosis.
XAI has divergent effects: it can help or paradoxically bias interpretation depending on the user.
Clinicians and lay people respond very differently to the same AI explanations.

papers.title: Follicular Lymphoma Transformation is Characterized by Cytokine-associated Remodeling of Stromal and Macrophage Compartments.
papers.authors: Haradhvala NJ, Yiu SPT, Beckmann L, Sadigh S, Leibowitz Z, Landolsi E, Rivero S, Deng SL, Hu S, Zhang M, Filip D, Pospistle A, Yeo YY, Maurer K, Gustafsson J, Stewart K, Shanmugam V, Van Orden M, Lu WS, Li S, Livak KJ, Qiu H, Basak A, Shalek AK, Danysh BP, McDonough M, Gohil SH, Ren Y, Zhou Y, Neuberg DS, Tyekucheva S, Rodig SJ, Jacobsen ED, Mraz M, Murakami MA, Kurt H, Wu CJ, Getz G, Jiang S, Parry EM.
papers.abstract: Across cancer, one of the most frequent examples of histologic transformation is the evolution of follicular lymphoma (FL) to an aggressive large cell lymphoma. Despite recent progress, understanding of the molecular and cellular underpinnings of transformation remains incomplete. Here, we dissect the interplay of tumor and microenvironment cell populations across transformation through a multimod
summary_bullets: Multimodal profiling dissects tumor-microenvironment interplay during transformation of follicular lymphoma to aggressive large-cell lymphoma.
Transformation is characterized by cytokine-driven remodeling of stromal and macrophage compartments.
Identifies microenvironmental changes as active drivers, not just bystanders, of lymphoma transformation.

papers.title: Feline mammary carcinomas display evidence of stemness, epithelial-mesenchymal plasticity, and metastasis-associated M2-like macrophage infiltration
papers.authors: Bakhle, K. M., Nelissen, S. R., Duhamel, G. E., Dongre, A.
papers.abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is the most aggressive subtype of breast cancer-a consequence of high proliferation rates, stemness, epithelial-mesenchymal plasticity, and immune evasion. Feline mammary carcinomas (FMCs) are spontaneous mammary gland cancers associated with high rates of metastasis and death. The aggressive biological behavior of FMCs, as well as their lack of expression of h
summary_bullets: Feline mammary carcinomas exhibit stemness, epithelial-mesenchymal plasticity, and M2-like macrophage infiltration, mirroring triple-negative breast cancer.
FMCs show high metastatic potential and aggressive behavior similar to human TNBC, supporting their use as translational models.
M2 macrophage infiltration may contribute to immune evasion in FMCs, relevant to understanding TNBC progression.

papers.title: Longitudinal single cell RNA-sequencing of Pik3caH1047R-driven mammary tumorigenesis reveals coordinated transformation of epithelial and fibroblast transcriptional states
papers.authors: Le, J. T., Kim, E. K., Srivastava, V. T., Nakagawa, R., Phong, K. T., Childree, G., Moser, B. A., Goga, A., Gartner, Z. J.
papers.abstract: Breast cancer is a heterogeneous disease in which a single oncogenic driver can give rise to divergent tumor phenotypes. How oncogenic mutations generate epithelial state plasticity and coordinately remodel the surrounding tissue remains incompletely understood. Here, we applied longitudinal single cell RNA-sequencing to trace the mammary landscape during Pik3caH1047R-driven tumor progression in t
summary_bullets: PIK3CA mutation drives coordinated transcriptional changes in both epithelial tumor cells and surrounding fibroblasts during mammary tumorigenesis.
Single oncogenic driver generates epithelial state plasticity through dynamic transcriptional reprogramming observable at single-cell resolution over tumor progression.
Tumor microenvironment remodeling occurs synchronously with epithelial transformation, suggesting integrated cell-cell communication during malignant development.

papers.title: The effect of melittin intervention on murine cervical cancer cells: An in-depth proteomics investigation
papers.authors: zhang, r., wang, M., zhang, k., zhuo, H., li, S., jiang, J., qiu, J., chen, D., Yan, T., guo, R.
papers.abstract: Melittin, the principal bioactive peptide of bee venom, exhibits promising antitumor activity, whereas its molecular mechanisms in cervical cancer remain incompletely understood. In this study, the biological effects and molecular responses of melittin in U14 cervical cancer cells were investigated using Astral data-independent acquisition (Astral-DIA)-based quantitative proteomics combined with m
summary_bullets: Melittin induces cervical cancer cell death through multiple molecular pathways identified via advanced quantitative proteomics analysis.
Astral-DIA proteomics reveals previously unknown mechanisms of melittin's antitumor activity in U14 cervical cancer cells.
Bee venom peptide melittin shows potential therapeutic application for cervical cancer treatment with defined molecular targets.

papers.title: Pharmacological arginine deprivation renders pancreatic cancer cells susceptible to senolysis and inhibition of the integrated stress response
papers.authors: Mainz, L., Sarhan, M. A. F. E., Schlicker, L., Kirner, S., Morton, J., Gerhard-Hartmann, E., Rosenwald, A., Eilers, U., Schuelein-Voelk, C., Schmitz, W., Baluapuri, A., Eilers, M., Wolf, E., Diefenbacher, M., Schulze, A., Rosenfeldt, M. T.
papers.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is almost inevitably fatal and largely resistant to current chemotherapy regimens. Senolysis, i. e. the selective elimination of senescent cells, and the targeting of cancer specific cellular metabolism are two novel treatment approaches that have proven to be effective for a variety of cancer types in pre-clinical studies. We now demonstrate that pharmacolo
summary_bullets: Arginine deprivation induces senescence in pancreatic cancer cells, making them vulnerable to senolytic drugs and ISR inhibitors.
Combined targeting of arginine metabolism and senescent cell elimination offers a novel therapeutic strategy for treatment-resistant PDAC.
This approach exploits cancer-specific metabolic dependencies to overcome chemotherapy resistance in pancreatic cancer.

papers.title: Patient-Derived Liver Cancer Organoids Reflect Tumor Biology and Their Growth Phenotype Correlates with Clinical Outcomes
papers.authors: Kim, Y. S., Go, Y.-H., Kim, H. S., Seo, J., Kim, D. o., Hwang, D.-Y., Yang, W., Lim, J. H.
papers.abstract: Liver cancer remains a major global health burden with high mortality and limited treatment response prediction tools. Patient-derived cancer organoids have emerged as promising preclinical models that recapitulate tumor heterogeneity; however, the biological significance of morphological diversity within established organoids remains poorly characterized in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). In this
summary_bullets: Patient-derived liver cancer organoids recapitulate tumor heterogeneity and biology.
Organoid growth phenotype (morphological diversity) correlates with clinical outcomes in hepatocellular carcinoma.
Positions organoid growth patterns as a potential predictive biomarker.

papers.title: Synergistic cytotoxicity with Chk1/Chk2-inhibitor prexasertib in small cell lung cancer following lurbinectedin-induced G2/M-checkpoint activation
papers.authors: Uruchurtu, A. F. S. S., Su, A. Y., Ganga, H., Zhang, S., Raissi, A., Kwon, K., Tummala, T., Roady, T., Moreno, J., Dubielecka-Szczerba, P. M., Azzoli, C. G., El-Deiry, W. S.
papers.abstract: Small cell lung cancer (SCLC) is an aggressive thoracic malignancy with a 5-year survival rate under 7%. Lack of meaningful improvement of survival rates despite advances in treatment highlights the need for novel therapeutic approaches to improve patient outcomes. Currently, carboplatin + etoposide chemotherapy is the backbone of treatment for most patients. Lurbinectedin is a cytotoxic drug with
summary_bullets: Lurbinectedin induces G2/M checkpoint activation in SCLC cells; combining with Chk1/Chk2 inhibitor prexasertib produces synergistic cytotoxicity.
Checkpoint inhibition strategy overcomes SCLC resistance to standard carboplatin/etoposide chemotherapy.
Novel lurbinectedin-prexasertib combination offers potential therapeutic advancement for aggressive SCLC treatment.

papers.title: Longitudinal structural variant phylogenies define tumor evolution under therapeutic selection pressure in metastatic prostate cancer
papers.authors: Liu, Y., Lai, J., Yang, Y., Markowski, M. C., Antonarakis, E. S., De Marzo, A. M., Yegnasubramanian, S., Wood, L. D., Sena, L. A., Karchin, R.
papers.abstract: Therapeutic pressure shapes tumor evolution by selecting for subclones with distinct genomic architectures. In metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC), structural variants (SVs) are central to this process but rarely incorporated into clonal reconstruction from bulk DNA sequencing. We describe SVCFit, a computational framework that estimates the cellular fraction of diverse SV clas
summary_bullets: SVCFit framework enables phylogenetic reconstruction of tumor evolution using structural variants from bulk sequencing data in metastatic prostate cancer.
Structural variants serve as key genomic markers tracking clonal selection under therapeutic pressure in castration-resistant prostate cancer.
SV-based clonal analysis reveals distinct tumor subpopulations and evolutionary pathways not captured by traditional mutation-only approaches.

papers.title: Comprehensive transcriptomic profiling uncovers an inflammatory maturation program conserved in human and mouse dendritic cells
papers.authors: Bourque, J., Kousnetsov, R., Hawiger, D.
papers.abstract: Conventional dendritic cells (cDCs) integrate signals to balance tolerance and immunity, but how steady-state cDC programs are changed during inflammatory maturation remains incompletely resolved. Here, using Seqtometry-based analysis of mouse and human cDCs, we identify distinct steady-state cDC1 gene programs enriched for either tolerance-associated or immune response-associated (pre-immunogenic
summary_bullets: Inflammatory maturation of dendritic cells involves coordinated shifts from tolerance-promoting to immune-activating gene programs conserved across species.
Seqtometry analysis reveals distinct steady-state cDC1 subprograms that are dynamically remodeled during maturation.
Cross-species transcriptomic comparison identifies conserved maturation mechanisms between human and mouse dendritic cells.

papers.title: Gut-Associated Metabolites (GAMs) revitalize dysfunctional CD8⁺ T lymphocytes in Osteosarcoma
papers.authors: SAPRA, L., Bhardwaj, A., Paladhi, A., Farhat, A., Kaur, T., Kaur, S. P., Saini, C., Kumar, V. S., Khan, S. A., Srivastava, R. K.
papers.abstract: Osteosarcoma (OS) is one of the top ranking and deadliest primary malignant bone tumor of youngsters and adolescents. OS has poor prognostic features due to its immunosuppressive "cold" tumor microenvironment, obstructing the anti-tumor effector functions of immune cells (including cytotoxic CD8 T lymphocytes). Recent developments have focused on the role of Gut Microbiota in modulating effector i
summary_bullets: Gut-associated metabolites restore CD8⁺ T cell function in immunosuppressive osteosarcoma microenvironment.
Gut microbiota metabolites combat osteosarcoma's "cold" tumor phenotype through immune cell activation.
GAMs represent potential therapeutic target to enhance anti-tumor immunity in osteosarcoma patients.

papers.title: Want to get more from AI? Treat every prompt like an experiment
papers.authors: Dewar JM.
summary_bullets: Nature commentary argues researchers should approach AI prompting with the same rigor as a scientific experiment.
Encourages systematic testing and iteration to get more reliable, useful outputs from AI tools.

papers.title: Uncovering ectopic GC-like niches for tumor reactive lymphocyte priming in lung adenocarcinoma using Stereo-XCR-seq
papers.authors: Zhan X, Huang M, Zhang Y, Liu Z, Liu C, Guo Y, Liu Y, Zhou W, Yan Y, Zeng H, Dong Y, Dong X, Chen X, Yang H, Ma R, Zhu F, Zheng X, Li X, Hou S, Gao Z, Yin J, Chan FK, Wu Q, Deng S, Yao Y, Suo S, Liu C, Liu L, Xu X, Hou Y, Tao H, Ai X, Dong Y, Zeng T, Sun H, Li Y, Zuo L, Wang H, Liu X, Wu Z, Zhou J, Zeng Z, Feng Y.
papers.abstract: T/B cell receptors (T/BCR), coordinating antigen-targeting immune response, play crucial roles in anti-tumor immune response. Tracking T and B cell clonal evolution in situ at single-cell resolution is essential for understanding the adaptive immune responses. To address the lack of tools for in situ single-cell T/BCR (XCR) sequencing, we develop Stereo-XCR-seq, an efficient method for retrieving
summary_bullets: Develops Stereo-XCR-seq, an in situ single-cell method for spatially resolved T/B-cell receptor (TCR/BCR) sequencing.
Reveals ectopic germinal-center-like niches in lung adenocarcinoma that prime tumor-reactive lymphocytes.
Enables tracking of clonal immune cell evolution directly within the tumor microenvironment.

papers.title: A foundation model for sleep-based risk stratification and clinical outcomes
papers.authors: Bilal E, Araujo MLD, Beck KL, Heinzinger CM, Ghosn S, Saab CY, Foldvary-Schaefer N, Rogers JL, Mehra R.
papers.abstract: Clinical sleep studies capture multiple physiologic signals, yet interpretation is often reduced to single summary measures of limited prognostic value, such as the apnea-hypopnea index. We present a foundation model that learns rich representations of sleep physiology from more than 10,000 clinical sleep recordings linked to electronic medical records. Here we show that sleep physiology contains
summary_bullets: Built a foundation model trained on over 10,000 clinical sleep recordings linked to electronic medical records.
Moves beyond single summary metrics (like apnea-hypopnea index) to richer sleep-physiology representations.
Enables better risk stratification and prediction of clinical outcomes from sleep data.

papers.title: Ultrarapid deep 3D histology enables intraoperative mapping of glioma infiltration
papers.authors: Liu Z, Li Y, Chen L, Wei M, Wei M, Sun Y, Wang T, Cheng H, Liu X, Ji M, Shi L.
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) histology provides volumetric insights into tissue microarchitectures across entire specimens, holding great promise for more accurate prognostication. However, existing methods are too slow for intraoperative consultations. We present ULTRA (ultrarapid cleared stimulated Raman with AI), a label-free, stain-free, fixation-free, and section-free platform that leverages the ch
summary_bullets: ULTRA is a label-free, stain-free, fixation-free 3D histology platform using stimulated Raman scattering plus AI.
Fast enough for intraoperative use, unlike existing 3D histology methods.
Enables real-time mapping of glioma infiltration margins during surgery.

papers.title: Privacy risks from medical AI tools are not shared equally
papers.authors: Zhang H, Ghassemi M.
summary_bullets: Nature commentary highlights that privacy risks from medical AI tools fall disproportionately on certain patient groups.
Calls attention to equity considerations often overlooked in medical AI deployment and data use.

papers.title: This AI Raygun can shrink and supersize proteins - opening the door to easy editing
papers.authors: Conroy G.
summary_bullets: News piece on "Raygun," an AI tool that can shrink or enlarge natural proteins while preserving function.
Framed as opening new possibilities for easier, more flexible protein engineering.

papers.title: SPEN Loss Drives Extrafollicular Diffuse Large B-cell Lymphoma with Female-Specific Lethality and Therapeutic Vulnerabilities
papers.authors: Pelzer B, Meydan C, Spiegel IM, Karagiannidis I, Xia M, Teater M, Welter EM, Searcy ZE, Hilton LK, Barisic D, Fong A, Fa P, Sethi S, Isgor IS, Fielding JJ, Karbalayghareh A, Burdette CS, Tumuluru S, Debek SM, Lee S, Massoni-Badosa R, Durmaz C, Salataj E, Pararajalingam P, Chen Z, Pelzl RJ, Shah S, Rivas MA, Hoehn KB, Mlynarczyk C, Isles HM, Wang X, Dogan A, Elenitoba-Johnson KSJ, Scott DW, Dreval K, Morin RD, Leslie CS, Puri R, Geri JB, Chin CR, Chadburn A, Mason CE, Reinhardt HC, Anguera MC, Béguelin W, Venturutti L, Melnick AM.
papers.abstract: Diffuse large B-cell lymphomas (DLBCL) are genetically and phenotypically heterogeneous, making diagnosis and treatment challenging. Current models suggest DLBCLs derive from follicular B cells engaged in adaptive immune responses. By studying cooccurring truncating mutations in SPEN and NOTCH2 in the BN2-DLBCL subtype, our data suggest a previously unrecognized extrafollicular trajectory. Using a
summary_bullets: SPEN and NOTCH2 co-occurring truncating mutations define a previously unrecognized extrafollicular DLBCL trajectory.
This SPEN-loss DLBCL subtype shows female-specific lethality.
Identifies therapeutic vulnerabilities specific to this newly defined lymphoma subtype.

papers.title: Same-Slide Spatial Multiomics Integration with IN-DEPTH Reveals Tumor Virus-Linked Spatial Reorganization of the Tumor Microenvironment
papers.authors: Yiu SPT, Chang Y, Yeo YY, Qiu H, Wu W, Michel HA, Jin X, Huang R, Kure S, Parmelee L, Luo S, Cramer P, Lee JL, Wang Y, Zhao Z, Yeung J, El Ahmar N, Simsek B, Mohanna R, Van Orden M, Lu WS, Livak KJ, Li S, Gao C, Burgess M, Keane C, Shahryari J, Kingsley LG, Al-Humadi RN, Nasr S, Nkosi D, Sadigh S, Rock P, Frauenfeld L, Kaufmann L, Zhu B, Basak A, Dhanikonda N, Chan CN, Krull J, Cho YW, Chen CY, Brown J, Wang H, Zhao B, Lee JJ, Loo LH, Kim DM, Boussiotis VA, Zhang B, Wei K, Shalek AK, Howitt BE, Signoretti S, Schürch CM, Hodi FS, Burack WR, Rodig SJ, Ma Q, Jiang S.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics and proteomics have enabled profound insights into tissue organization, yet these technologies remain largely disparate, and emerging same-slide multiomics approaches are limited in plex, spatial resolution, signal retention, and integrative analytics. We introduce IN-situ DEtailed Phenotyping To High-resolution transcriptomics (IN-DEPTH), a streamlined, resource-efficient,
summary_bullets: IN-DEPTH combines spatial transcriptomics and proteomics on the same tissue slide, improving on disparate single-modality methods.
Reveals tumor-virus-linked spatial reorganization of the tumor microenvironment.
Designed to be streamlined and resource-efficient for broader adoption.

papers.title: CellTune: an integrative software for accurate cell classification in spatial proteomics
papers.authors: Bussi Y, Shainshein D, Ovits E, Posner S, Azulay N, Maimon N, Keidar Haran T, Ben-Uri R, Brown C, Schuldiner N, Yaniv E, Van Valen D, Milo I, Elhanani O, Schiemann R, Keren L.
papers.abstract: Spatial proteomics measures multiple proteins in situ, capturing tissue complexity. However, cell classification in densely packed tissues remains challenging because of the lack of efficient classification algorithms, annotation tools and high-quality labeled datasets to benchmark computational methods. We introduce CellTune, an integrated software for analysis of large spatial proteomics dataset
summary_bullets: CellTune is integrative software for accurate cell classification in densely packed spatial proteomics data.
Addresses the lack of efficient algorithms, annotation tools, and benchmark datasets in the field.
Aims to standardize and improve cell-type calling across spatial proteomics platforms.

papers.title: SpaMTP: integrative statistical analysis and visualization of spatial metabolomics and transcriptomics data
papers.authors: Causer A, Lu T, Kriel J, Moffet JJD, Fitzgerald CCJ, Newman A, Vu H, Tan X, Vo T, Cui C, Narayana VK, Whittle JR, Best SA, Freytag S, Nguyen Q.
papers.abstract: Spatially resolved multimodal data enable the exploration of transcriptional, proteomic and metabolic regulation, yet analytical tools to integrate these spatial omics modalities, particularly spatial metabolomics, remain limited. We developed SpaMTP, an end-to-end framework that implements functions within a common Seurat architecture. It introduces analyses for metabolite annotation, joint clust
summary_bullets: SpaMTP integrates spatial metabolomics and transcriptomics analysis within the familiar Seurat framework.
Adds tools for metabolite annotation, joint clustering, and cross-modality visualization.
Fills a gap left by existing tools that don't handle spatial metabolomics well.

papers.title: Author Correction: Cucurbituril-based anion-conducting membranes with supramolecular nanopores
papers.authors: Xu Z, Lin D, Yin H, Feng Q, Foglia F, Zhen Y, Morris A, Berrod Q, Pang M, Huang L, Liu J, Tian J, Wang X, Yang C, Tang X, Zhang X, Wang B, Wang H, Liu K.
summary_bullets: Published correction to a paper on cucurbituril-based anion-conducting membranes with supramolecular nanopores.
No new scientific findings; amends or clarifies details of the original report.

papers.title: End-to-end multimodal pathology foundation model with clinical dialogue
papers.authors: Vorontsov E, Shaikovski G, Casson A, Viret J, Zimmermann E, Tenenholtz N, Wang YK, Bernhard JH, Godrich RA, Retamero JA, Shia J, Gonen M, Weiser MR, Klimstra DS, Yousfi R, Fusi N, Fuchs TJ, Severson K, Liu S.
papers.abstract: Recent rapid progress in the field of computational pathology has been enabled by foundation models. These models are beginning to move beyond encoding image patches toward whole-slide understanding, but their clinical utility remains limited. Here we present PRISM2, a multimodal slide-level foundation model trained on 2.3 million whole-slide images and 14 million question-answer pairs derived fro
summary_bullets: PRISM2 is a multimodal, slide-level pathology foundation model trained on 2.3M whole-slide images and 14M Q&A pairs.
Moves beyond patch-level image encoding toward whole-slide, dialogue-capable understanding.
Aims to improve clinical utility of computational pathology through interactive, clinically grounded outputs.

papers.title: Scientists using LLMs will 'do more, less well', modelling study predicts
papers.authors: Glickman K.
summary_bullets: Modelling study predicts scientists using LLMs will increase output but reduce quality/rigor per study.
Raises concerns about an AI-driven productivity/quality trade-off in research.

papers.title: Mapping micrometastatic seeds of relapse
papers.authors: Yeo HTG, Tan IB.
papers.abstract: In this issue of Cancer Cell, Liu et al. apply spatial multi-omics to map colorectal cancer micrometastases across primary tumors and matched liver and lung metastases, revealing liver micrometastases as an early evolved, stem-like, immune-suppressed residual disease state linked to a six-gene recurrence signature.
summary_bullets: Commentary on a study applying spatial multi-omics to colorectal cancer micrometastases in liver and lung.
Liver micrometastases appear as an early, stem-like, immune-suppressed residual disease state.
This state links to a six-gene signature predicting recurrence risk.

papers.title: Spatial atlas of the human brain vasculature reveals specialized cell ensembles
papers.authors: Wang JC, Sanchez D, Arul S, Gülsuyu B, Gopinadhan A, Mukhtar T, Kim J, Andrews JP, Alonso Cee Williams M, Jung Y, Hashimoto ML, Kim CN, Bhalla S, Ewing-Crystal NA, Bernabei JM, Letchuman V, Haddad AF, Hemphill K, Weinsheimer SM, Kim H, Narsinh KH, Cooke DL, Cadwell CR, Wälchli T, Elahi FM, Yang AC, He P, Chang EF, Molofsky AB, Winkler EA.
papers.abstract: The brain vasculature comprises diverse specialized cells that are essential for brain function, yet their spatial organization remains poorly understood. Here, we construct a comprehensive cerebrovascular cell atlas encompassing 314,535 transcriptomes that captures the arteriovenous axis and defines consensus cell states. We then perform spatial transcriptomics to map 1,529,740 cells across the h
summary_bullets: Built a cerebrovascular cell atlas of over 314,000 transcriptomes spanning the human brain's arteriovenous axis.
Spatial transcriptomics mapped over 1.5 million cells to their vascular locations across the brain.
Reveals specialized, spatially organized vascular cell ensembles supporting brain function.

papers.title: AI-driven discovery and validation of a GIPC1 PDZ domain inhibitor for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
papers.authors: Rachamala HK, Rao Nakka NM, Angom RS, Varanasi SM, Wei F, Kulkarni T, Dutta SK, Wang E, Kulkarni NM, Geoffrey A S B, Hegde SP, Perumal S, Gurram K, Gharibi H, Gaetani M, Mukherjee SP, Babiker H, Pal K, Mukhopadhyay D.
papers.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains highly aggressive, with a five-year survival rate under 13.3%, due to late diagnosis, rapid progression, and therapeutic resistance, highlighting the need for advanced treatments. GAIP-interacting protein C terminus 1 (GIPC1), a scaffolding protein overexpressed in PDAC, drives tumor growth and chemoresistance but has remained "undruggable" due to it
summary_bullets: GIPC1, an "undruggable" scaffolding protein, drives PDAC tumor growth and chemoresistance.
Used AI-driven discovery to find a small-molecule inhibitor targeting GIPC1's PDZ domain.
Validates a new therapeutic candidate for a cancer with under 13.3% five-year survival.

papers.title: Human-inspired time-series health evaluation with an adaptive multimodal electronic skin
papers.authors: Xu C, Zheng H, Heng W, Liu R, MarionSims J, Li J, Jin P, Tay RY, Min J, Wang G, Yue Y, Gao W.
papers.abstract: Electronic skin powered with artificial intelligence could enable next-generation robotic and medical devices, yet integrating multimodal sensors and analyzing heterogeneous, multifrequency time series remain challenging. Most wearable machine learning architectures are time-invariant and trained for a specific task, limiting transfer across modalities and users. We present a multimodal electronic
summary_bullets: Developed a multimodal, AI-powered electronic skin for time-series health monitoring.
Adaptive architecture transfers across sensing modalities and users, unlike prior time-invariant wearable ML.
Enables human-inspired, continuous health evaluation for next-gen wearable and robotic devices.

papers.title: Inference of secreted protein signaling activities in intercellular communication
papers.authors: Ru B, Gong L, Yang E, Park S, Zaki G, Aldape K, Wakefield L, Jiang P.
papers.abstract: The human genome encodes ~1,900 secreted proteins, many of which mediate intercellular communication. Secreted proteins do not act cell-autonomously, limiting systematic approaches to characterize their functions. Here we introduce SecAct (Secreted Activity, https://secact.ccr.cancer.gov ), a computational framework that infers the signaling activities of 1,170 human secreted proteins from spatial
summary_bullets: SecAct infers signaling activity of 1,170 human secreted proteins from spatial and transcriptomic data.
Addresses the challenge that secreted proteins act non-cell-autonomously, complicating standard analysis.
Provides a computational framework and public tool for studying intercellular communication via secreted factors.

papers.title: Author Correction: Sleep chart of biological ageing clocks in middle and late life
papers.authors: MULTI Consortium, O'Toole CK, Song Z, Anagnostakis F, Yang Z, Tian YE, Duggan MR, Zou C, Leng Y, Cai Y, Bai W, Fu CHY, Rafii MS, Aisen P, Wang G, De Jager PL, Zeng J, Oh HS, Zhou X, Walker KA, Belsky DW, Zalesky A, Simonsick EM, Resnick SM, Ferrucci L, Davatzikos C, Wen J.
summary_bullets: Published correction to a large multi-cohort study of biological ageing clocks across middle and late life sleep.
Amends details of the original "sleep chart of biological ageing clocks" report.

papers.title: Mediators of cell fate decisions in human fetal kidney development identified using spatial transcriptomics
summary_bullets: Nature Genetics piece on mediators of cell fate decisions in human fetal kidney development, identified via spatial transcriptomics.
Companion to related work directly mapping kidney developmental cell-fate decisions.

papers.title: Single-cell spatial mapping of human kidney development implicates the microenvironment in guiding cell fate decisions
papers.authors: Levinsohn J, Grindel S, Dumoulin B, Abedini A, Conte C, Huang AZ, Levin-Klein R, Weisz B, Rabinowitz G, Bergeson AM, Ha E, Klötzer KA, Zhang N, Titchenell P, Li M, Park JS, Arroyo JP, Finn LS, Sasaki K, Beckerman P, Pleniceanu O, Romagnani P, Hughes AJ, Susztak K.
papers.abstract: Evolution has used cell-cell communication as a strategy to coordinate organ development, enabling the reproducible generation of intricate structures. Classically, these interactions have been studied one at a time in model organisms, limiting our understanding of how cellular interplay coordinates human development. We investigated human kidney development using single-cell RNA sequencing and sp
summary_bullets: Single-cell RNA-seq plus spatial profiling of human kidney development reveals cell-cell communication driving fate decisions.
Shows the microenvironment actively guides which cell fates progenitor cells adopt.
Moves beyond model-organism studies to directly characterize human kidney developmental signaling.

papers.title: Decadal sink-source shifts of forest aboveground carbon since 1988
papers.authors: Qian Z, Bathiany S, Liu T, Blaschke LL, Teo HC, Boers N.
papers.abstract: Forest ecosystems are vital to the global carbon cycle, yet their long-term aboveground carbon (AGC) dynamics remain uncertain. Here, we integrate multi-source satellite observations with probabilistic deep learning models to reconstruct a harmonized, uncertainty-aware global forest AGC record from 1988 to 2021 at 0.25<sup>∘</sup>. We find that, although global forests sequestered 6.2 PgC, moist t
summary_bullets: Combined satellite data with probabilistic deep learning to reconstruct global forest carbon dynamics from 1988-2021.
Global forests sequestered 6.2 PgC overall, but moist tropical forests show shifting sink/source behavior.
Provides an uncertainty-aware, long-term record of how forest carbon storage is changing.

papers.title: Escaping our own biases: AI, scientific reasoning, and discovery in molecular biology
papers.authors: Costa TRD, Penadés JR.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence may transform molecular biology not by always providing the correct answer, but by exploring mechanistic possibilities unconstrained by the assumptions that shape expert thinking. Its greatest contribution may be exposing the intellectual blind spots of scientists, while experimental validation remains the ultimate arbiter of truth.
summary_bullets: Commentary argues AI's value in molecular biology may lie in exploring possibilities beyond expert assumptions, not just giving correct answers.
AI can expose scientists' intellectual blind spots, but experiments remain the final arbiter of truth.

papers.title: Spatiotemporal multiomics uncover tumor ecosystem dynamics during metastatic colonization
papers.authors: Sun Y, Zhong Y, Liu S, Zhang Z, Wang C, Liu Y, Chen J, Guo W, Gu X, Rao K, Wang Z, Cao M, Wang Y, Huang W, Zou X, Chen X, Qiu S, Shi Y, Sun H, Huang X, Wang Y, Wang J, Wu Z, Tian R, Zhang Y, Gu J, Jiang M, Bai Y, Li G, Xie M, Xi F, Peng L, Liu S, Yang S, Zhang Y, Esteban MA, Jin X, Chen A, Wang J, Cang Y, Peng DH, Xu X, Zhou J, Wu L, Fan J.
papers.abstract: The mechanisms underlying the interactions between disseminated tumor cells (DTCs) and their tissue microenvironment during metastatic colonization are currently poorly understood. We integrated multimodal single-cell and spatial profiling from liver cancer mouse models and human metastases to track the spatiotemporal dynamics of DTCs and their microenvironments from single-cell seeding to overt l
summary_bullets: Integrated single-cell and spatial profiling of liver cancer mouse models and human metastases.
Tracks disseminated tumor cells and their microenvironment from single-cell seeding to overt metastasis.
Reveals dynamic tumor-microenvironment interactions driving metastatic colonization over time.

papers.title: Gene regulatory innovations from transposable elements in primate cerebellum development
papers.authors: Yamada T, Sepp M, Sarropoulos I, Kaessmann H.
papers.abstract: Transposable elements are hypothesized to have driven gene regulatory innovation, yet their contributions to primate brain development at the cell type level remain underexplored. Here, we use single-cell multiomics data from human, macaque, marmoset, and mouse cerebella to show that transposable element contributions to different cell types are shaped by varying degrees of constraints across cell
summary_bullets: Compared single-cell multiomics across human, macaque, marmoset, and mouse cerebellum development.
Transposable elements contribute to gene regulatory innovation in a cell-type-specific manner.
Degree of TE-driven regulatory contribution varies with evolutionary constraint across cell types.

papers.title: Deep learning segmentation with curvature consistency reveals astrocyte nanostructure across species
papers.authors: Fok AHK, Wang Y, Ng M, Syed T, Wong TYM, Salmon CK, Salathiel T, Grondin-Eddy W, Fan L, Siddiqi K, Murai KK.
papers.abstract: Cellular function depends on the precise deployment and distribution of nanoscale structures, but these features remain difficult to measure and compare between cells and datasets. This challenge is pronounced for astrocytes, whose intricate nanostructures interface with neurons, glia, and vasculature, to control brain development, synaptic development/plasticity, homeostasis, and responses to inj
summary_bullets: Developed a curvature-consistent deep learning segmentation method for nanoscale cell structures.
Applied to astrocytes, whose fine nanostructures are hard to measure and compare across datasets and species.
Enables cross-species comparison of astrocyte nanostructure relevant to brain development and disease.

papers.title: Miniaturizing and modifying natural proteins with Raygun
papers.authors: Devkota K, Shonai D, Mao J, Ko YS, Wang W, Soderling S, Singh R.
papers.abstract: Proteins have evolved over billions of years through coordinated substitutions, insertions and deletions, yet computational protein design cannot fully replicate nature's ability to engineer new proteins from existing templates. Protein language models<sup>1-3</sup> generate informative per-residue representations, but harnessing them for large-scale, function-preserving sequence modifications has
summary_bullets: Raygun uses protein language model representations to enable large-scale, function-preserving protein redesign.
Can miniaturize or otherwise modify natural proteins while retaining their function.
Advances computational protein engineering beyond fixed per-residue predictions.

papers.title: Parallel nonlinear neuromorphic computing with temporal encoding
papers.authors: You G, Qian C, Wu O, Chen H.
papers.abstract: The proliferation of deep learning applications has intensified the demand for electronic hardware with low energy consumption and fast computing speed. Neuromorphic photonics have emerged as a viable alternative to process high-throughput information at the physical space. However, the simultaneous attainment of high linear and nonlinear expressivity poses a considerable challenge due to the powe
summary_bullets: Demonstrates parallel nonlinear neuromorphic computing using temporal (time-based) encoding.
Neuromorphic photonics offer a low-energy, high-speed alternative to conventional electronic hardware.
Addresses the tradeoff between linear and nonlinear expressivity in photonic neuromorphic systems.

papers.title: Integrating structurally defined DNA-carbon nanotube sensors with machine learning for cancer detection
papers.authors: Chen P, Zheng X, Li Y, Li J, Zhou X, Wen Y, Liu J, Wang P, Li X, Chen R, Lin Z.
papers.abstract: Liquid biopsy is a promising, noninvasive approach for cancer detection, but current methods often trade off accuracy, operability, and cost. To address these limitations, we introduce an artificial perception system (APS) for liquid biopsy that combines a structurally defined DNA-carbon nanotube sensor array with machine learning (ML) models. The array produces multichannel fluorescence fingerpri
summary_bullets: Built an "artificial perception system" combining DNA-carbon nanotube sensor arrays with machine learning.
Produces multichannel fluorescence fingerprints for noninvasive liquid biopsy cancer detection.
Aims to improve on existing liquid biopsy methods that trade off accuracy, ease of use, and cost.

papers.title: Organelle proteomics of human, neonatal pig, healthy and diabetic mouse islets
papers.authors: Caliskan ÖS, Haas DT, Ferreira JV, Chubanava S, Kemter E, Cota P, Bastidas-Ponce A, Tarquis-Medina M, Czarnecki O, Bhattacharya S, Jaki J, Geiger V, Kakimoto P, Brandt D, Sachser M, Dürr C, Delgado de la Herran H, Cebrian-Serrano A, Müller TD, Wolf E, Lickert H, Bakhti M, Krahmer N.
papers.abstract: Pancreatic islets, in which β cells constitute 50%-80% of the endocrine mass, are the body's site for glucose-regulated insulin secretion.
